Equations of Motion of a Rigid Body                                                                              Summary and Exercises


                                        Summary

        The motion of a rigid body relative to an arbitrary inertial frame of reference is described by the following
         system of ordinary differential equations:

                                  dP     dM
                               = F,    = K,                                       (1)
                                                   dt          dt

         where P is the total linear momentum of the rigid body, M is its total angular momentum, F = P f is the
           total force applied to it, and K = P[r × f] is the total torque of the forces acting on the body.
          For given forces and torques, these equations allow one to determine the evolution of the dynamic characteristics
         P(t) and M(t) during the motion. However, this information does not automatically imply knowledge of the
          behavior of the kinematic characteristics (the body’s position and velocity).
          Since the total linear momentum of any mechanical system is related to the velocity of its motion as a whole
       Vc (i.e., the velocity of its center of mass) and the radius vector of the center of mass RC by the relations

                                                 dRc
                             P = µVc = µ        ,
                                                                   dt

         where µ is the total mass of the body, the translational equations of motion for the momentum easily yield
          the equations
                                   dVc          d2Rc
                                  µ   = F  or  µ    = F,
                                                 dt               dt2
          the solutions of which directly give the evolution of these kinematic characteristics.

Equations of Motion of a Rigid Body                                                                              Summary and Exercises


                                        Summary

        As for any mechanical system, the total angular momentum of a rigid body is composed of its intrinsic
          angular momentum Ms (defined as the angular momentum relative to the center-of-mass frame) and the
           orbital angular momentum Morb = Rc × P, i.e.,

                    M = Ms + [Rc × P].

          Substituting this relation into the rotational equations of motion for the rigid body, we find the equation for
          the evolution of the proper angular momentum:

                                 dMs
                                = K −Rc × F.
                                                    dt

        To solve a problem involving rotational motion, one must relate the angular momentum to the angular
           velocity via the inertia tensor, and the angular velocity to the Euler angles via the Euler kinematic equations.
           Alternatively, one can use any other three independent angles and their corresponding kinematic relations.

       When using the Lagrangian approach, six generalized coordinates are introduced: three coordinates of the
          center of mass and three angles (typically the three Euler angles). To then express the kinetic energy in
         terms of the angles and their time derivatives, it is necessary to use the kinematic relations between the
         components of the angular velocity and the angles.

                                        Homework

     Task HW8.07
    A thin channel is drilled along the generatrix of a homogeneous circular cone of mass M, whose axis is vertical
     and vertex is pointing upward. The cone is given an initial angular velocity Ω0 about its axis, and simultaneously,
     a small ball of mass m is dropped into the top opening of the channel without any initial velocity relative to the
     cone.

    What will be the angular velocity of the cone at the moment the ball exits the channel?


     Task HW8.08
    A symmetric top rotates about a fixed point that coincides with its center of mass. It is subjected to resistance
      forces from the surrounding medium, the moment of which about this point is K = −µΩ, where µ = const > 0
     and Ωis the angular velocity of the body.

     According to what law does the angular velocity of the body change?

     Hint 1: use dynamic Euler equations

     Hint 2: to integrate the system of equations, introduce a complex variable ξ = Ω1 +iΩ2, where i is the imaginary
      unit
